Subject: Post-call recap & next steps: embeddings integration

Hi Samir --

Thanks for your time today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery:

- Goal: migrate search/semantic ranking from ProviderX embeddings to Redwood embeddings for your knowledge base (~3.2M docs).
- Key constraints: vector dim compatibility (ProviderX uses 1536 dims), want to keep <1s query latency for top-K retrieval, batch ingestion pipeline with ~500k docs/day, ability to rerank with a lightweight transformer reranker.
- Questions we have: preferred storage (your vector DB vs Redwood-managed), whether you need per-tenant model pinning, current normalization/embedding preprocessing (L2 / cosine), and any downstream reranker features.

Next steps:
1) You'll share a sample export (1k docs) so we can run a small migration profile.
2) We (Priyom + Eng) will prepare an ingestion guide with batching recommendations and a migration plan that preserves vector dims and gives fallback options.
3) Setup a short tech sync early next week to review auth (API key vs OIDC), SDK snippet, and expected token / cost estimates.

Attachments: redwood_embeddings_migration_guide.pdf (migration checklist), token_usage_estimate.xlsx (rough cost model)

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa -- this is helpful.

We can share a 1k doc sample by EOD tomorrow. A couple of clarifications:
- ProviderX embeddings are 1536-d float32, no normalization on our side currently (we rely on cosine search which does implicit normalization in the vector DB).
- Our current ingestion batches are ~10k/day but we're planning to scale to 500k/day in Q4, so batching advice is critical.
- For routing, earlier infra expects us to host vectors in Pinecone; we are open to Redwood-managed vector store if it simplifies the migration and reduces operational load.

I'll loop in Lena (engineering) for the tech sync; she prefers Wed 9am PT if that works.

Best,

Hi Samir / Lena --

Quick answers ahead of the tech sync:

- Vector dimensions: Redwood supports multiple dims; we can produce 1536-d embeddings to match ProviderX for a drop-in experiment. If you want to switch dims (e.g., 1024 for cost/perf), we recommend reindexing and running an A/B evaluation.

- Normalization: since your vector DB does cosine similarity, you can either keep raw float32 vectors and rely on the DB's cosine, or we can normalize on ingest (L2) -- normalization helps with mixed-dimension/reranking pipelines. Our migration guide includes an option to normalize and store an additional normalized vector if you want to preserve both.

- Batching: for 500k docs/day we recommend chunking at 5k-10k per request with concurrency of 4-8 workers; Redwood batching SDK supports streaming ingestion with automatic backoff. We'll include code snippets for Node and Python.

- Migration path: 1) sample run with 1k -> eval recall/latency; 2) pilot 50k with side-by-side rerank; 3) full migration with phased cutover and rollback to ProviderX if needed.

I'll bring a short SDK snippet and auth options to the Wed sync.

Thanks,
Priyom
